newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Arsonists burn tonnes of Jamaica sugar, gov't says.
newsitem.headline: Arsonists burn tonnes of Jamaica sugar, gov't says.

text.p: Jamaican government officials Wednesday said arsonists in recent weeks have burned cane fields that would have yielded some 1,500 tonnes of sugar, for losses of US$645,000 by last weekend.
Most of the fires took place near the Frome sugar factory in western Jamaica. Officials said they suspected disgruntled sugar workers were setting the fires.
Jamaican sugar producers were forced to lay off nearly 1,000 workers in 1996, most of them at Frome, which is mechanizing its harvesting to save money.
"The government is adamant that proper investigations will be carried out to determine those responsible and restore proper order to the industry," Agriculture Minister Horace Clarke said.

Jamaica expects to earn US$100 million from sugar exports this year, down from the US$110 million in 1996. The fall in earnings is due to a 10 pct price reduction in the European Union, due to the strengthening of Sterling against the dollar.
